evidence: The hunk shows `captureFace` doing `try { return await createLocalVideoTrack(); } catch {` with the error object dropped, so a hardware fault and a denied permission were indistinguishable. The agent kept the intended null-return semantics and added `console.warn(..., error)`, which matches the reviewer's minimum fix.
guidance_note: When an optional capability degrades to null on failure, bind and log the caught error in the same edit that writes the catch; a bare `catch {}` is never the honest-absence form.

narrative: One finding against an empty catch in the new webcam capture path. The agent accepted it, kept the optional-track null return and logged the real error, and round 1 approved with nothing new. The second round only reviewed the fix.
guidance_observations: The agent's own doc comment cited [LAW:no-silent-failure] directly above a catch that discarded the error, so the law was named without being checked against the code under it.

evidence: The action's contract is `Promise<MenuAuthorResult>` and every other refusal is a typed arm, but `readOffers` threw on non-JSON or a non-array, which escapes `useActionState`'s rendering. The agent added the `malformed-submission` arm the reviewer proposed and rendered it in the form. The reply-hint says pushback, but the reply opens 'Valid — agreed'.
guidance_note: When a function's declared return is a result union, route edge-parse failures through a new arm of that union instead of throwing; check every `throw` in a server action against its declared result type before committing.

narrative: One finding: a thrown parse error bypassed the server action's typed result channel. The agent agreed, added a `malformed-submission` arm, kept the failure visible instead of turning it into an empty menu, and round 1 approved. No fix-caused findings.
guidance_observations: The original throw was written to satisfy one law (never wipe the menu silently) without checking it against the action's own declared outcome type. A typed arm satisfied both laws from the start.

evidence: `isVisible().catch(() => false)` inside `expect.poll` turns a page crash or a closed context into a generic poll timeout, as claimed. Instead of narrowing the catch, the agent removed the reload-poll entirely, arguing that the viewer navigates only after go-live and that the earlier `assertLiveVideo` proves the room is live. The agent reported the acceptance smoke passing at 23.9s after the change.
guidance_note: Before writing a retry or reload loop in a test, find the actual cause of the miss (here a `\bLIVE\b` regex that could not match `LIVE1`); a speculative retry is what pulled in the error-swallowing catch.

narrative: One finding against `.catch(() => false)` in an e2e poll. The agent removed the whole speculative reload-poll and used a direct `toBeVisible`, which removed the swallow at its source. Round 1 approved and did not repeat its earlier advisories as blocking.
guidance_observations: The retry wrapper was added before the real cause of the failure was known, and its error swallowing was the only finding. Diagnose first, then decide whether a retry is needed.

evidence: The README row still read 'auth.ts sets trustHost=false in production' while the same PR changed auth.ts to `trustHost: true`. Commit 7c8bde1 rewrote that row to describe trustHost:true plus the edge middleware.

evidence: The gcp-vm.sh comment said 'auth.ts sets trustHost=false in production for exactly this reason', which the auth.ts change contradicted. The 7c8bde1 diff replaces it with the trustHost=true / middleware model.

The `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` swap is a cheap, standard fix, but citing no-silent-failure for an error that was already thrown misapplies the law.
This duplicates F1: the same README row contradicts `trustHost: true`, and the reviewer correctly says the docs and the code cannot both be right. The 7c8bde1 README rewrite covers it.

evidence: The real hurt is that the comment claimed an ingress owned the host boundary while gcp-vm.sh exposes port 80 directly. The cure is wrong: the agent reports that an explicit `trustHost: false` in production threw UntrustedHost on every request even with AUTH_URL set, which matches Auth.js v5 non-Vercel behavior. The agent kept trustHost:true and added a middleware host allowlist derived from AUTH_URL, reporting that a live `Host: evil.com` got 400.
guidance_note: When a comment claims a boundary is enforced elsewhere ('the ingress owns the host boundary'), check the deploy artifact in the same PR for that enforcer before writing the claim.

evidence: This is the same trustHost=false doc drift as F1, raised from the auth.ts side. The 7c8bde1 rewrites of the README row and the gcp-vm.sh comment resolve it.

evidence: `-e AUTH_SECRET='${AUTH_SECRET}'` inside an unquoted heredoc breaks the generated VM script if the value contains a single quote, and the script only checks that the value is set. The 7c8bde1 `esc()` helper (`sed "s/'/'\\\\''/g"`) yields the standard `'\''` escape for every interpolated secret. This is a quoting and injection issue, not a swallowed error, so the no-silent-failure citation does not fit.
guidance_note: When generating a script with an unquoted heredoc, escape every caller-supplied value interpolated into a quoted position, or pass values through a channel that needs no quoting.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 7c8bde1 did not touch the Dockerfile, and the chdir comment and `CMD ["node", "apps/web/server.js"]` predate review. The premise that server.js may not chdir is refuted by the agent's own live check that identity.db and moderation.db land on /var/lib/crowdship-data. The agent still changed WORKDIR/CMD as 'hardening', and that edit is what drew F23 the next round.
guidance_note: When live evidence refutes a finding's premise, push back with that evidence instead of shipping a 'hardening' edit for an assumption the evidence just confirmed.

evidence: The middleware is new code from F6's fix in 7c8bde1. The agent refuted the build-time-inlining claim live: a forged Host got 400, which an inlined undefined would have let through as 200. The 'lazily memoized, robust by construction' hardening adds nothing against inlining: the original `allowedHost()` already read `process.env.AUTH_URL` per request, and inlining would rewrite the expression wherever it runs.
guidance_note: When pushing back with decisive evidence, don't add a 'robust by construction' change unless it addresses the mechanism the reviewer named; a memo does not change whether process.env is inlined.

evidence: The middleware added for F6 in 7c8bde1 does parse `new URL(authUrl)` on every request. 'Wasted CPU and GC pressure' overstates the cost of one URL parse. The 670fa48 memo (hostComputed/cachedHost) is a small, correct change.

The flag is a false positive: 7c8bde1 changed only the README image tag and the AUTH_URL row, and the `set -a; . .env.local` / `AUTH_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32) ./deploy/gcp-vm.sh` lines date from the original PR. Run in sequence, they regenerate the signing key on every deploy and log out every user, as claimed. 670fa48 split them into first-deploy and later-deploy flows. The reply-hint says pushback, but the reply accepts.
guidance_note: When documenting a deploy procedure, separate one-time setup steps (generating a secret) from every-deploy steps, and walk the documented commands once as a redeploy.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 7c8bde1 changed only the IMAGE docstring line, and the header listing LIVEKIT_* under 'Required env' is original PR content. Only AUTH_SECRET has a `:?` guard and the app falls back to the in-memory broker, so the header misstated the contract. 670fa48 moved LIVEKIT_* to Optional.
guidance_note: When writing a script's env-contract header, derive 'required' from the `:?` guards actually in the script.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: `--service-account="breadly@${PROJECT}..."` is original script content that 7c8bde1 did not touch. The README prerequisite list omitted that account, and 670fa48 added it with the Artifact Registry Reader and Logs Writer roles.
guidance_note: When listing a script's one-time prerequisites, enumerate every external resource name the script references (IP, firewall tag, registry, service account).

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the 'one persistent disk... survive a container replacement' prose is original README content. gcp-vm.sh runs `gcloud compute instances delete` and then creates a new instance with a fresh boot disk, so the store resets on every deploy. 670fa48 added a durability caveat stating this.
guidance_note: When documenting durability, trace the data path through the deploy script's own delete/create steps, not only through container restarts.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 7c8bde1 changed only the `outputFileTracingRoot` derivation, and the `transpilePackages` list is pre-existing, anchored outside the diff. The predicted failure on un-transpiled workspace TS does not occur: the agent reports the build passing and the deployed app exercising market.ts imports from @crowdship/ledger, menu, and others. The packet shows no build log, so that rests on the agent's report.

The finding exists only because F15's fix in 670fa48 changed `CMD ["node", "apps/web/server.js"]` to `WORKDIR /app/apps/web` + `CMD ["node", "server.js"]`. The premise is false: the pre-review CMD already located server.js at /app/apps/web, and the agent confirmed live that `/app/apps/web/server.js` exists, `/app/server.js` does not, and the site serves 200. The fix introduced no defect, but it cost a round-2 thread.
guidance_note: A refuted premise should be answered with the evidence, not with a speculative edit that puts a new changed line in front of the next review round.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 670fa48 did not touch next.config.mjs. This re-raises F22 on the unchanged `transpilePackages` line, which the reviewer itself calls 'a pre-existing omission'. The agent again cites the passing build and live use of those imports.

narrative: Round 0 raised 14 findings, 8 of them one doc-drift: the agent flipped auth.ts to `trustHost: true` and left the README and gcp-vm.sh saying trustHost=false. There were also three copies of a v1/v2 image-tag mismatch, all fixed in 7c8bde1. F6's fix added a host-allowlist middleware, which drew F16 (refuted live) and F17 (a minor memo). Most other round-1 findings (F18-F22) sat on original PR content the round-0 reviewer missed, so the flags on them are false positives. In round 1 the agent accepted F15 as 'hardening' even though its own evidence refuted the premise, and that Dockerfile edit drew the false F23 in round 2. Rounds 1 and 2 would have run anyway because real non-fix-caused findings (F18-F21) needed fixing.
guidance_observations: Half of round 0 was one stale fact repeated across files; one grep for `trustHost=false` before opening the PR would have removed 8 findings.
Twice (F15, F16) the agent had live evidence refuting the premise and still shipped a 'hardening' change; one of those changes drew a fresh round-2 finding.

Round 1 found several real bugs in content that round 0 had already read (F18 secret regeneration, F21 durability), so the reviewer's coverage varies between rounds; the agent cannot rely on round 0 being exhaustive.
